keyVerseText: Wherefore the well was called Beerlahairoi ; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered. Beerlahairoi: that is, The well of him that liveth and seeth me
rootMeaning: The root word בְּאֵר (bᵉʼêr) primarily denotes a pit or well, emphasizing a source of water essential for life. The etymology of בְּאֵר לַחַי רֹאִי combines בְּאֵר (well), חַי (living), and רֹאֶה (seer or one who sees), rendering the phrase as "well of the living One who sees me." This literal sense conveys more than a physical water source; it evokes a place intimately connected with divine life and personal divine observation.
usageInScripture: The term בְּאֵר לַחַי רֹאִי appears three times in Scripture, consistently referring to a specific location west of Kadesh, known as Beerlahairoi. The top translations—'Beerlahairoi,' 'of the well Lahairoi,' and 'the well Lahairoi'—reflect a stable understanding of the term as a proper name tied to a well. This consistency underscores its identity as a significant geographical and theological landmark rather than a generic term.
theologicalSignificance: The name בְּאֵר לַחַי רֹאִי reveals profound theological truths: it identifies God as the living One who actively sees and cares for His people. This well symbolizes not only physical sustenance but also spiritual life and divine presence. Recognizing God as the 'Living One seeing me' affirms His personal knowledge and ongoing involvement in the believer's life, reinforcing trust in His providence and intimate care. This understanding enriches faith by portraying God as both life-giver and vigilant protector.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 16:14 states, 'Wherefore the well was called Beerlahairoi; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered. Beerlahairoi: that is, The well of him that liveth and seeth me.' This verse highlights the well's name as a declaration of God's living presence and His attentive watchfulness over Hagar. The phrase בְּאֵר לַחַי רֹאִי encapsulates the reassurance that God is not distant but personally aware, offering both physical provision and spiritual comfort.
